speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal antibody and nerve stimulation results effectively rule out Myasthenia Gravis. Given your progressive gait disturbance, incontinence, and speech difficulties with negative structural and metabolic workups, have you noticed any significant weight loss or fatigue? Also, do you experience a "stuck" feeling in your throat or difficulty swallowing solids?

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal EMG and CSF results have ruled out myasthenia gravis, muscular dystrophy, vitamin deficiencies, thyroid disease, and most common inflammatory demyelinating conditions like multiple sclerosis. Given the progressive quadriparesis, incontinence, and dysarthria with a completely normal structural workup, have you noticed any subtle cognitive changes, personality shifts, or early morning leg stiffness and pain?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent infections, fever, weight loss, vision changes or seizures.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The comprehensive negative workup including normal CSF, EMG, and metabolic panels makes Multiple Sclerosis, compressive myelopathy, and neuromuscular junction disorders unlikely. Given the insidious onset of progressive quadriparesis, urinary incontinence, and bulbar symptoms (speech difficulty) in a 54-year-old male with no structural lesions, do you have any history of back pain, or do your legs feel stiff or painful specifically in the morning?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Kennedy's Disease (Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy)
